item.title: Tong: CT Issued Dozens Of Warnings Of Data Privacy Act In 2025
item.description: Key changes highlighted in the report include stronger protections for minors’ data, broader definition of sensitive data, and new disclosure requirements related to artificial intelligence.

item.title: Lamont Outlines Plan To Provide Universal Free Breakfast, Expand Free Lunch To CT Students
item.description: The FY2027 budget proposal that Lamont presented to the Connecticut General Assembly at the opening of the legislative session on Wednesday includes $12 million in funding to provide free breakfast to all of the state’s K-12 public school students, and also includes $500,000 to eliminate all fees for those who qualify for reduced-price lunches.

item.title: CT Creates $330M Fund To Respond To Potential Federal Cuts To State Programs
item.description: Majority Leader Jason Rojas of East Hartford acknowledged that the fund had been established to allow the state to react while the legislature was not in session — and had included specific language expiring when the General Assembly reconvened. He said though that the ability to respond to federal actions quickly was paramount.

item.title: Connecticut’s Small Towns Press Lawmakers For Relief At COST’s Annual Meeting
item.description: At the Connecticut Council of Small Towns’ annual Town Meeting last week, municipal leaders from across the state delivered a blunt message: the cost of running local government is rising faster than small towns can sustain.

item.title: Today’s Toons
item.description: Editorial cartoons by John Darkow & Milt Priggee

item.title: Opinion | The Most Unfit Man To Occupy the White House – Ever
item.description: Columnist Barth Keck says he fears that the typical “level-headed” and “reasonable” manner journalists and politicians have typically taken when analyzing the behavior of Donald Trump ignores what is now, to him, an obvious fact: The man is a cruel and selfish boor unfit to lead any country in the world, let alone the United States of America.

item.title: State Investigating After Three Die In Custody In Same Week
item.description: “My deepest sympathies go out to the families of those who passed,” said Department of Correction Commissioner Angel Quiros. “These tragic incidents affect all those involved very deeply. I assure you that the safety and well-being of those under our supervision remains a fundamental priority.”

item.title: CT Republican Leaders Condemn State Investigation Into 2025 Police Deadly Force Incident
item.description: In a statement, three Republican leaders from the state House of Representatives, Minority Leader Vincent Candelora of North Branford, Greg Howard of Stonington and Tammy Nuccio of Tolland criticized the decision to investigate the incident. Howard is a police officer and House ranking member of the Public Safety and Security Committee. Nuccio is ranking member of the Appropriations Committee and the mother of a Connecticut state trooper.

item.title: Connecticut Lawmakers, Housing Providers Seek $123.9M To Address Rising Homelessness
item.description: The Connecticut Coalition to End Homelessness released its 2026 legislative agenda Friday, seeking roughly $123.9 million annually to expand rental assistance, prevention programs, emergency shelter capacity, and supportive housing services amid federal funding uncertainty.

item.title: CT Investigating 500-Unit Apartment Complex After Town Issues Evacuation Orders Over Conditions
item.description: Attorney General William Tong has opened an investigation into Concierge Apartments management, sending a civil investigative demand under the Connecticut Unfair Trade Practices Act seeking documentation and answers regarding the landlord’s management and response to deteriorating conditions at the Rocky Hill apartment complex.
